name: Mohsen Ghaemmaghami
title: Senior Software Engineer
pitch: I build fast, clean, scalable web applications. 12+ years of frontend and full-stack work, from a 1-million-user ranking page in 2013 to module-federated React platforms today.
openTo: Open to senior frontend / full-stack roles, remote or AU

highlights: Building commerce platforms on Medusa with Node.js, Redis and TypeScript.
Designed and shipped real-time features over WebSocket for a community platform, in Node.js and TypeScript.

Restructured the frontend with module federation and a pnpm + nx monorepo, with a unified type-safe contract between DB, backend and frontend: 35% less deployment complexity, 30% more developer efficiency, 90% fewer manual errors.
Rewrote the main Editor app with React Query, Tailwind and an in-house Storybook design system: 40% smaller bundle, better error handling.
Raised test coverage 25% with Playwright, and pushed the marketing site's Core Web Vitals above 90 across the board.
Mentored new joiners (two became tech leads) and took part in hiring.
Prototyped a gRPC/ConnectRPC contract between backend and frontend.
Built a DeFi browser extension on ether.js and the Compound Finance SDK.
Introduced TDD with Jest, React Testing Library and Storybook: 90% fewer bugs, faster releases.
Rewrote the legacy product in Next.js, Tailwind and HeadlessUI: 25% faster loads.
Led a team of 20 engineers; the marketplace product doubled sales by rethinking the user journeys.
Doubled team velocity with a synchronized dev environment, 80%+ aligned with production.
Architected the React + Redux + SSR frontend: 30% faster loads, TTFB ~130 ms, FCP 1.6 s, LCP 2 s.
Shipped the iOS and Android apps with React Native.
Built an SEO-friendly site on WordPress with custom PHP landing pages.
Kept the blog at ~0 downtime on nginx.
Produced a web-development course that reached thousands of learners on DVD (it was 2015; YouTube wasn't the classroom yet).
Ran the site, landing pages and campaigns: +20% conversion, +40% engagement.
Built and maintained Varzesh3.com's frontend, one of Iran's most visited sites.
Real-time live scores over WebSocket with long-polling fallback: under 1 second from pitch to screen.
Built Anten.ir's live video streaming platform with Vue, Vuex and HLS.js.
Engineered the AngularJS admin panel, streamlining editorial workflows by 30%.
Started as a PHP developer; grew into head admin and development lead.
Built a game-player ranking platform for 1M+ users at 98% uptime, integrated with BMI.ir's customer club.

lines: I can center a div. Vertically. On the first try. With Tailwind, in one class.
I know the difference between margin and padding, and more importantly, when the answer is gap.
I use <button> for buttons and <a> for links. It is remarkable how much accessibility that buys.
My Tailwind class strings are longer than some commit messages, and far more honest.
skills.serious: HTML5, CSS3, SASS, Tailwind CSS, responsive and accessible UI since 2012.

lines: I know why 0.1 + 0.2 isn't 0.3, and I know when it's fine not to care.
I know what `this` refers to. The answer is "it depends who called", which is the whole lesson.
typeof null === "object" has been a bug since 1995. I've learned to work around older things than that.
I can explain the event loop on a whiteboard, and debug it with a flame chart.
I can write a regex. I also write a comment above it, for the person I'll be in six months.
skills.serious: ES2024+, performance profiling, bundling, the platform APIs. 12+ years.

lines: `any` is a loan with interest. I take it out rarely and pay it back fast.
I know the difference between type and interface. I also follow whatever the codebase already does.
I've written types strict enough that the compiler caught a bug the tests missed. That's the point of them.
I can read a four-parameter generic without lying down afterwards.
skills.serious: Strict TypeScript across frontend and Node, end-to-end typed contracts (gRPC/ConnectRPC).

lines: I know the difference between useCallback and useMemo, and I know the best optimisation is usually neither.
I know why your list needs a key, and why the array index is not it.
I've never called a hook conditionally. The Rules of Hooks are the only rules I've never wanted to break.
Wild RE-RENDER appeared! MOHSEN used React.memo. It's super effective.
I've built a design system in Storybook that cut a bundle by 40%. Components with a story ship with fewer surprises.
skills.serious: React since 2017: architecture, design systems, Storybook, performance, micro-frontends.

lines: I know where 'use client' goes, and more importantly, where it shouldn't.
Hydration mismatches don't scare me. They're just the server and the client disagreeing about the time.
skills.serious: Next.js app and pages routers, SSR/SSG, rewrites of legacy products.

skills.serious: React Query, Redux, GraphQL, REST, gRPC/ConnectRPC.
